clue.text: New Honda cycle? It's a gem

indicators.note: something new is made over, so the letters of the car name and the bike word are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a fresh Honda motorbike counts as a treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal on HONDA CYCLE, whose ten letters rearrange to give the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalcedony is a semi-precious quartz used for carving and jewellery, so it is a kind of precious stone.

clue.text: One with energy, good at coming up with capital

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the run of pieces is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
E is the physics symbol for energy
PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lively, capable person is praised for producing money for a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns the whole string I, E, PI, AT, so IEPIAT is read upwards. 'capital' looks like money but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Taipei is the seat of government of Taiwan, so it is a national capital city.

clue.text: A variety of papers I assess

indicators.note: a variety is a different arrangement, so the letters of the newspaper word and the pronoun are mixed up

explanation.surface: A critic sets about judging a range of newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: A is kept as it is; 'variety of' signals an anagram of PAPERS I, giving PPRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise something is to judge its value or quality, the same as evaluating it.

clue.text: Quarrel in Malibu, stupidly

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone describes a foolish row breaking out on the California coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across maliBU STUPidly. Malibu is a beach town in California.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is an informal word for a noisy argument or falling-out.

clue.text: Surprise when rubbish is found to contain nickel

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

indicators.note: the rubbish word holds the chemical symbol inside it

parts.note: tosh is British slang for nonsense or rubbish
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: A scrap merchant is startled to find a valuable metal in a heap of junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' is the source of letters, not a comment on the find: the British slang word for nonsense opens to take the metal symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze them, a strong form of surprise.

clue.text: See space below ring in part of cooker

indicators.note: in a down clue, the pieces placed below come after the ring piece

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
v, from Latin vide, is the abbreviation meaning see in reference books
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: An instruction points to the area under a hotplate on a stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below' puts V and EN under O in this down entry. A ring is also a hob burner, which pulls the solver towards the cooktop.
explanation.definitionFit: The oven is the enclosed baking compartment of a cooker, so it is one component of it.

clue.text: Call to reduce speed which people start to applaud

parts.note: who asks which people, as in 'who came?'

indicators.note: the start of the following word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A compere signals the crowd to slow down as the clapping begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes the first letter of applaud, A, after WHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call used to make a horse slow down or stop.

clue.text: Eloquent endorsement put about by European backing society in republic

indicators.note: in an across entry, the reversed endorsement and the E come behind, after, the first group
the society letter goes inside the country name

parts.note: Peru is a South American republic

indicators.note: put about means turned round, so the endorsement word is read backwards

parts.note: a visa is an official endorsement stamped in a passport

explanation.surface: A political campaign in a South American country wins Europe's support with a smooth slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put about' turns the endorsement backwards; 'by' sets E beside it, and 'backing' puts that group behind the republic holding S. Peru is the republic here.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquent speech is fluent and convincing, so it is persuasive.

clue.text: Strong characters in court after strike favouring reconciliation

indicators.note: the court group follows the strike and favouring pieces

parts.note: to rap is to strike sharply
pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the strong men are placed inside the court abbreviation

parts.note: he-men are strong, macho characters

explanation.surface: In a courtroom, tough figures who once struck out now favour making peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strong characters' looks like bold type but means he-men; 'in' sets them inside the court abbreviation, and 'after' puts that group behind strike and favouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapprochement is a French loanword for the re-establishing of friendly relations, especially between nations.

clue.text: Clown getting suitable censure for idiosyncratic nonsense

indicators.note: for means in place of, so the new pieces replace the idiosyncratic word inside the clown word

parts.note: something idiosyncratic is your own, peculiar to you
apt means suitable
a rap is a rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A circus clown is given a fitting telling-off for his eccentric silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals that OWN, from 'idiosyncratic', is swapped out of CLOWN, leaving CL, and APT plus RAP go in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is showy, empty talk, so it means rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Troublesome heckler's tips intermittently interrupting prime minister?

indicators.note: intermittently means at intervals, so the two letters do not go in side by side but at separate points
the heckler's letters break into the name of the prime minister

parts.note: Tony Blair was UK prime minister, so Tony stands for a prime minister

indicators.note: the tips of the heckler's word are its first and last letters, the heckler's opening and closing sounds

explanation.surface: A heckler keeps breaking into a prime minister's speech, causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts the first and last letters of heckler's into TONY, and 'intermittently' spaces them out, so the R lands a place further on than the H. The question mark flags a prime minister named only by first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorny problem is one full of difficulties, like a stem covered in prickles.

clue.text: Sign made of stone in Italy

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone
taken as written
I is the international vehicle registration letter for Italy

explanation.surface: A zodiac symbol is said to be carved from Italian marble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' means a sign of the zodiac, not a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is the third sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Trojan, having no answer, crushed by substantial retaliation

indicators.note: the Trojan piece is squeezed inside the substantial word

parts.note: real means solid or substantial

indicators.note: the answer letter is removed from the Trojan prince

parts.note: Paris was a prince of Troy

explanation.surface: A Trojan warrior, lost for a reply, is overwhelmed by a heavy counter-attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed by' means squeezed inside: the shortened prince sits within the word for substantial. Paris is the prince who carried off Helen and started the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprisal is an act of revenge or retaliation against an enemy.

clue.text: Gruff quality displayed by sailor going over point in 16 letter 4 on ship

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Gruff quality displayed by sailor going over point in 16 letter 4 on ship': AB + NESS need RUPT, which '16 letter 4' (SPORADIC's fourth letter, R) cannot give; the cross-reference looks misread (perhaps letters 3-6 of 20, IRRUPT) and no scan or reprint confirms it.
annotationWithheld.clue: Gruff quality displayed by sailor going over point in 16 letter 4 on ship

clue.text: Bird eyes tractor with agitation, making nest for companion

indicators.note: the shuffled letters wrap round the companion abbreviation as a nest holds an egg
agitation stirs things up, so the letters of eyes and tractor are rearranged

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A bird glares at a farm vehicle in alarm while building a home for its mate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with agitation' shuffles eyes and tractor into OYSTERATER, and 'making nest for' wraps those letters round the companion abbreviation, as a nest holds an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The oystercatcher is a black-and-white shorebird with a long orange bill.

clue.text: Irregular soldiers restricted by police operations getting upset

indicators.note: the soldiers are hemmed in by the upturned police and operations pieces
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the police and operations run is read upwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
ops is short for operations
RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers

explanation.surface: Unorthodox troops are hemmed in by police actions and become distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns police and operations, CID OPS, upwards into SPODIC before the soldiers go in. 'Irregular soldiers' looks like a single phrase but splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic happens at irregular intervals, now and then.

clue.text: Person putting up scaffolding in street, having to climb, sets off

indicators.note: the scaffolder sits inside the reversed street abbreviation
in a down clue, climbing means reading upwards, so the street letters are turned

parts.note: a rigger erects scaffolding or ship's rigging

explanation.surface: A scaffolder working in the road has to go up the poles before starting the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to climb' turns the street abbreviation upwards in this down entry, giving TS, and 'in' sets the scaffolder between its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Triggers is a verb meaning starts or sets in motion, as setting off an alarm does.

clue.text: Unknown number enthralled by cold, confident person commanding attention

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the unknown and number go inside cold and confident

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
sure means confident
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: A mystery figure is captivated by a cool, self-assured star who draws all eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralled by' means held captive by: the unknown and number sit inside the cold-plus-confident pair. 'cold, confident person' reads as one description but splits three ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynosure is the centre of attention or admiration, someone everyone looks at.

clue.text: Nut developed on shrub? Not right

indicators.note: something developed has changed form, so the letters of nut are rearranged

parts.note: rue is an aromatic evergreen shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a nut has grown on a bush, and is told it is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' turns NUT into UNT, followed by RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means false, so a statement that is untrue is not correct.

clue.text: With support, ignoring saint, first of troops burst in

indicators.note: the saint abbreviation is left out of the support word

parts.note: a stirrup is a rider's foot support

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Troops, backed up and showing no respect for a holy man, storm a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes ST from STIRRUP, leaving IRRUP, and 'first of' adds T from troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to enter forcibly or suddenly, to break in.

clue.text: Government for example maintained by elevated ruler

indicators.note: maintained by means held up by, so the example piece sits inside the ruler
in a down clue, raised up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an emir is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A government is propped up by a ruler who has been promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns the ruler upwards in this down entry, giving RIME, the word for frost, which then holds the example abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system of rule, especially an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Sound candid in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that the word for candid is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: straight means frank or candid

explanation.surface: Someone describes a remark that is honest when said out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective or noise, but it means a narrow sea channel, as in Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow stretch of water joining two larger bodies, the same as a strait.

clue.text: Fine suggestion: 'the last shall be first'

indicators.note: the final letter of the suggestion word is moved to the front

parts.note: a hint is a suggestion

explanation.surface: A preacher offers a neat hint from the Bible quote about the last becoming first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last shall be first' moves the T of HINT to the start, the biblical phrase taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine and thin both describe something slender, as in fine thread.

clue.text: Delightful quip in opening needing no work

indicators.note: the quip goes inside what remains of the opening
the work abbreviation is dropped from the opening word

parts.note: taken as the word itself
OP, short for opus, is a musical work
a gag is a joke or quip

explanation.surface: A comedian's witty opening line works without effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no' drops the work abbreviation from opening, leaving ENING, and 'in' sets the quip inside. 'opening' reads as a comedian's first line but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Engaging means charming and attractive, so something engaging is delightful.

clue.text: Obstruction force smashed is rebuilt

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters of 'is rebuilt' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barrier knocked down by force is put back up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges IS REBUILT into ILIBUSTER, after F.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster is a tactic of long speeches used to block or delay a vote in a legislature.

clue.text: Hard problem returning with call to increase speed

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the hard and problem pieces are read backwards

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A dog-sled driver comes back to a tough problem and urges the team on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns H and SUM together into the shout a musher gives sled dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mush is the command given to sled dogs to start or go faster.
